text:
jamal: Hey @support, ACME integration started seeing intermittent 429 bursts since ~2026-02-22 14:05 UTC. Spike window 14:12-14:22. Example req id we got: x-rw-req-id=rq_8f3b2a9c. We're polling every 250ms from ~12 workers. Can you advise exact repro steps we should collect?

maya: thanks Jamal — can you paste a full response (headers + body) for one of the 429s and one successful request around the same time? Also need the client IP(s) and whether you use connection pooling.

jamal: attaching quick snippets below. client_ip=34.85.12.7. We do keep an HTTP/1.1 pool with 12 persistent connections. Sample curl we used to reproduce locally:

```bash
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"test"}'
```

And the server response for one of the 429s we captured: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-req-id: rq_8f3b2a9c
x-rate-limit-limit: 120
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 1765236738
retry-after: 8
content-type: application/json

{"error":{"message":"rate limit exceeded"}}
```

jamal: here's a tiny log snippet from our side around the spike (timestamps UTC):
```
[2026-02-22T14:11:58Z] outgoing req id=rq_local_01 status=200 latency_ms=34
[2026-02-22T14:12:07Z] outgoing req id=rq_8f3b2a9c status=429 latency_ms=12
[2026-02-22T14:12:08Z] outgoing req id=rq_local_05 status=429 latency_ms=10
[2026-02-22T14:12:09Z] outgoing req id=rq_8f3b2b1f status=200 latency_ms=45
```

oliver: good detail, thanks. Two quick asks from SRE: 1) capture the `x-rw-req-id` header for both 200s and 429s and paste them (we'll grep logs). 2) run the curl above with `-v` so we see the full TLS/HTTP exchange and all headers. Also include `--trace-ascii` if you can, so we get timing.

sophie: also helpful to know whether the requests are hitting the same model variant or if fallback routing is occurring. If you can add `X-RW-Client-Trace: true` header (temp) that will cause our proxy to echo routing in the response for debug.

jamal: will do. Running a noisy reproduce now with -c 6 concurrency from my laptop to simulate bursts. will paste results shortly.

ratebot: Automated alert: customer=acme-corp detected 52 429 responses in 10m window (2026-02-22T14:10:00Z - 2026-02-22T14:20:00Z). avg_retry_after=6s. Alert ID R-832.

maya: I'm checking account quota in the console now — can you confirm whether ACME has any reserved/dedicated capacity or is on hosted pay-as-you-go? Quota vs rate-limit semantics differ.

jamal: hosted pay-as-you-go. No reserved capacity. Billing shows normal usage, but I'll attach the usage graph.

sophie: quick reproduction suggestion for determinism: run two phases — 1) steady low qps (1 req/s) for 2m, 2) sudden burst: 30 req/s for 60s. Capture request ids. That pattern tends to trigger token-bucket style throttles.

jamal: results from my quick burst run (local):
```
# run: ab-style, 6 concurrent workers, 120 requests
-> 98/120 200
-> 22/120 429
Sample failed response header: x-rw-req-id=rq_8f3b7d4e retry-after=7
```

oliver: perfect. I'm filing a server-side log grep request: please provide a list of x-rw-req-id values for all 429s (comma-separated) and I'll attach to the infra ticket. Also include the approximate client timestamps for each id (so we can correlate across nodes).

jamal: here are ~10 from the failed run: rq_8f3b2a9c, rq_8f3b7d4e, rq_8f3b9aa1, rq_8f3c0123, rq_8f3c0456, rq_8f3c0789, rq_8f3c0abc, rq_8f3c0def, rq_8f3c10fe, rq_8f3c11aa. Local timestamps included in the CSV I'll attach.

maya: thanks — I'm also checking whether any billing limits (monthly usage cap) were hit briefly, but that generally returns a different error. This looks like a token-bucket rate limit on the hosted tier.

sophie: if infra finds the limit is enforced cluster-wide we should check our dynamic burst allowance config (burst_window_seconds, bucket_refill_rate). I'll join the ticket when available.

oliver: next steps from SRE: 1) Jamal to upload HAR + `curl -v` trace and the CSV of req ids (by 15:00 UTC). 2) Maya to confirm account capacity/quotas (ETA 20m). 3) SRE to grep logs + return with whether 429s are per-customer bucket or per-route global. 4) If needed, schedule 30m debug call.

jamal: uploading HAR and curl traces now (link: https://files.acme.internal/har/2026-02-22-acme-burst.har). let me know when you see them.

ratebot: Additional note: spike correlated with scheduled batch job starting at 14:11:57 UTC for acme-corp.

maya: saw the HAR. I can confirm all 429 responses include x-rate-limit-remaining: 0 and retry-after present. Looks like a quota exhaustion at that moment. I'm escalating to billing+infra to confirm whether a short-lived quota override occurred.

sophie: thanks all. If infra asks you to run a targeted reproduce against a staging token, please do so and include `-H \"X-RW-Client-Trace: true\"` and I'll collect traceback info.

jamal: ok will run staging reproduce and post results. Appreciate the quick triage :thumbsup:

maya: I'll update this thread when I have quota confirmation. If we need to raise short-term burst capacity for ACME while they refactor their polling pattern, we can do that as a one-off.

oliver: logging ticket created INT-1129, attached req ids and links to traces. marking SRE action item.

jamal: closing loop here for now — will ping if I see more 429s after reducing polling to 1s. Thanks!
